name: Acutaas Chemicals Ltd
title: Acutaas Chemicals Ltd - 543349 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Acutaas Q4 FY26 revenue rose 40.3% YoY to INR432.8 crores with EBITDA margin of 42.4%; FY26 PAT hit a record INR356.4 crores.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR432.8 crores, up 40.3% YoY, with gross margin of 62% (up 1,467 bps) and EBITDA of INR183.5 crores at a 42.4% margin. PAT was INR134.3 crores, up 114.1% YoY. For FY26, revenue was INR1,339.4 crores (+33%), EBITDA INR480.4 crores (about 2x) and PAT a record INR356.4 crores. Management guided to 25% revenue growth in FY27 and a similar EBITDA margin to FY26, while battery chemicals and semiconductors are still in investment phase.

financial_highlights.change: margin +1,487 bps YoY; more than 2x YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash and cash equivalents (31 Mar 2026)

segments.name: Advanced Pharmaceutical Intermediates (incl. CDMO)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR392.4 crores, up 43.9% YoY, driven mainly by CDMO; Q4 EBITDA margin about 44% per CFO. Core API portfolio reshuffle was mostly done in the first 9 months and the business grew sequentially in Q4.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals (incl. BFC semiconductor and commodity)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR40.3 crores, up 12.3% YoY; commodity sub-segment declined, offset by a strong BFC recovery. Q4 EBITDA margin about 29% per CFO, attributed to BFC's high-margin recovery.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 25%, measured on total FY26 revenue across all verticals; management said it would revise guidance if CDMO or electrolyte demand exceeds that later in the year.
EBITDA margin expected to stay at a similar level to FY26 (about 35% consolidated), not Q4 levels, as product mix is expected to be similar.
CDMO long-term guidance of INR1,000 crores revenue by FY28 reiterated on the call.
Battery chemicals and semiconductors expected to become self-sustaining growth engines by FY28.
Two additional battery chemical products expected at commercial scale in FY27; a third electrolyte additive capex to finish by Q1 FY27 and a fourth is in business development.
FY27 capex: about INR50 crores spillover from FY26 (electrolyte additive and pilot plant) plus about INR40 crores maintenance; R&D centre capex yet to be finalised.

Indichem JV (South Korea) facility expected to complete in H2 CY2026, earlier than the previously guided start of CY2027; management expects about 1x revenue relative to the INR200 crore capex, with margin not yet guided.
H1 typically contributes about 40% of annual revenue and H2 about 60%; management said this seasonality is expected to persist in FY27.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR195 crores, mainly Jhagadia battery chemical project, Sachin pilot plant and maintenance.
Electrolyte additive (Jhagadia): phase 1 complete; phase 2 due by Q1 FY27. Pilot plant at Sachin delayed by equipment arrival, now due by Q2 FY27.
Electrolyte additive capacity is 2,000 metric tons each for VC and FEC; management said the plant is fully covered by customer contracts for the next 3 years.
INR190 crores invested in Indichem Inc. (South Korea JV) in FY26; R&D centre there is operational and sample shipments to prospective customers have started.
Q4 FY26 utilisation: Sachin 75%, Ankleshwar Unit 2 31%, Jhagadia Unit 3 50%.
Planned R&D centre expansion targeting 10x capacity, covering pharma, battery, semiconductor, electronics and cosmetics; land acquisition under evaluation.
demand_pricing: Management said demand momentum is strong, with healthy inflow of new product inquiries and robust demand for existing products.
Gulf conflict has disrupted feedstock supply and shipping and pushed raw material prices higher; management says no raw material shortage is expected to affect production continuity.

CDMO: first product under a 10-year supply contract with a customer; four further validated products expected to add revenue in FY27, each with INR50-100 crores peak revenue potential. Ramp-up expected mainly in FY28 per analyst exchange.
Semiconductor shipments to Japanese and Korean customers have started; BFC recovered from Q4 FY26.
Spec chem ex-acquired sites grew 12-15% despite some price reduction; battery electrolyte additives expected to add meaningful FY27 revenue, ramping quarter by quarter.
Management said sodium-ion batteries are not a material threat to lithium-based demand; the company says it is targeting less than 1% of demand.

qa_highlights.question: Why is goodwill INR104 crores and how is it recoverable, given the Indichem JV has no revenue yet?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR48 crores relates to the earlier BFC acquisition goodwill; the rest arises because the JV partner's 25% stake was issued at par while Acutaas paid INR190 crores, so 25% of the investment is booked as goodwill. Management said it expects recoverability on the basis of future projections.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin split between Pharma and Specialty in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Pharma EBITDA margin was about 44% and Specialty about 29% in Q4. Abhishek said the specialty margin reflects BFC's high-margin recovery alongside traditional spec chem.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue potential and timelines for CDMO products beyond the first one?
qa_highlights.answer: Four more products are validated and commercialised, pending regulatory approval, with peak revenue of INR50-100 crores each. Management expects revenue from them in FY27, with more meaningful ramp in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Acutaas guiding 25% growth when Bayer guided about 50% growth for Fermion in CY2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 25% CAGR guidance, its track record for over a decade, and said it would revise guidance if business potential goes beyond that later in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will seasonality (weak Q1 with 20-30% QoQ decline) persist given the Fermion ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said Q1 has been lower than Q2, Q2 lower than Q3, and Q3 lower than Q4 for 15 years, due to a base of more than 600 customers and over 100 products. Management expects this pattern to continue in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 EBITDA margin stay at FY26 levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins should be similar to FY26 (around 35%) because product mix will stay similar, with electrolyte additive and CDMO additions offsetting each other. Q4's 42% margin is not a base case.

risks_watch: Raw material cost inflation and shipping disruption from the Gulf conflict could pressure margins despite guided stability.
Delays in the Sachin pilot plant (now Q2 FY27) and electrolyte phase 2 (Q1 FY27) could push back battery chemical revenue.
CDMO revenue is concentrated in the Fermion contract; four other products await regulatory approval, and FY28 INR1,000 crore CDMO target depends on them.
Indichem JV has no revenue yet, and the INR104 crore goodwill recoverability depends on future projections.
Low utilisation at Ankleshwar Unit 2 (31%) and Jhagadia Unit 3 (50%) in Q4.
Working capital days rose to 120 from 114, with lower payable days.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and growth: management repeatedly reiterated 25% FY27 growth and the FY28 CDMO target. Answers were evasive on specifics such as battery chemical revenue, Indichem margins, and the Q4 margin's relevance to FY27. Management also acknowledged the Gulf-related cost pressure with caution.
key_quotes: I'm confident of delivering 25% revenue growth in FY '27.
We are confident in our ability to maintain EBITDA margin at a similar level in the coming year.
Q1 is typically our weakest quarter with revenue steadily increasing sequentially till Q4, which is always the strongest quarter.

adds.what: Electrolyte additive phase 2 at Jhagadia (2,000 MT each of VC and FEC; phase 1 complete)
Indichem Inc. (South Korea JV) facility, about INR200 crore capex
Two additional battery chemical products at commercial scale
R&D centre expansion targeting 10x capacity (land under evaluation)

growth.why: Management guides 25% FY27 revenue growth and a similar ~35% EBITDA margin, backed partly by electrolyte additive capacity fully contracted for 3 years, a CDMO product under a 10-year supply contract, and Indichem JV completion in H2 CY26; no firm capacity timeline or quantified order book for the full 25% was given, and the pilot plant slipped to Q2 FY27.
